risks.data_migration: 0010 is a data-only seed of 14 rows keyed on the UNIQUE category.slug, applied with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so a re-run is a no-op. downgrade deletes exactly those fourteen slugs (never TRUNCATE) and, because service.category_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, leaves service rows intact and merely uncategorised -- no orphans, no FK violation. The seeded slug set and count are asserted against CATEGORY_TAXONOMY inside the migration, so the seed can never drift from the product taxonomy.
risks.security_privacy: No new endpoint, no authentication surface, no user input path, no secret. Category is non-sensitive structural metadata declared in a non-secret example YAML.
risks.portability: No new runtime or test dependency and no Redis (Q6-A); PostgreSQL stays the only mandatory stateful service. The migration uses plain SQLAlchemy Core inserts. amd64/arm64 unaffected.
risks.zero_cost_safety: Category is NOT an offer fact and never affects Z0 classification, quotas, or the publication gate. It is declared configuration, never inferred: an undeclared service stays uncategorised and is honestly reported in the uncategorized rollup rather than guessed into a category. No free claim is created or strengthened by this slice.
risks.immutability: service.category_id is a mutable column on 'service'; trg_offer_version_immutable guards offer_version only; and category is absent from _stable_material_facts(), so content_hash is unchanged and re-publishing after categorisation mints NO new offer_version. This is asserted directly (offer_version count + every content_hash identical before/after) rather than assumed.
risks.regression: The only behaviour change to existing code paths is that a published service may now carry a declared category instead of always NULL, plus two integration seed helpers that must now resolve rather than re-insert the canonical Category rows 0010 seeds. The whole existing suite is re-run; the previously-skipped integration tests are additionally run for real against an isolated PostgreSQL.
risks.supply_chain: No new npm or Python dependency; pip-audit, npm audit and detect-secrets stay green.
